arguments.value: 12-year-old girl admitted with acute painful vulvar ulceration, burning, itching, dysuria, abdominal symptoms, fever, and inflammatory labs. Exam showed swollen, inflamed vulva with bleeding ulcers on the labia minora/majora, hymenal caruncle, and vestibulum; histology showed necrotic, purulent lesions without malignancy. Infectious workup was largely negative except HSV IgG positivity and significant pyuria/bacteriuria. Symptoms began shortly after the first Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine dose, and she had no sexual activity or prior genital disease. Treated with cefuroxime, topical silver sulfathiazole, and NSAIDs with gradual healing; lesions resolved completely by 60 days and she remained well at 1-year follow-up.
